newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Poor Turkmen grain crop revised up to 640,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Poor Turkmen grain crop revised up to 640,000 T.

text.p: Turkmenistan has revised upwards its 1997 net grain crop to 640,000 tonnes from a preliminary figure of 600,000 tonnes.
"The final figure for the 1997 gross grain harvest is 640,000 tonnes," an Agriculture Ministry official told Reuters.
The former Soviet republic had targeted this year's harvest at 1.2 million tonnes.
Yields this year averaged 1.56 tonnes per hectare compared to some 0.8 tonnes last year when the desert Central Asian state, which seeks self-sufficiency in grain, reaped a disastrous 480,000 tonnes.
The area sown to grain this year shrank to 400,000 hectares from around 600,000 hectares last year. Officials had hoped in vain for higher yields of 2.5-3.0 tonnes per hectare.
Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov has already sacked three regional heads and a deputy prime minister over the bad harvest.
Bread remains the main staple and is consumed in large quantities.
Interfax news agency, quoting grain specialists in the capital Ashgabat, said grain harvested this year would be enough to produce 320,000 tonnes of bread-making flour.
Turkmenistan consumes annually 750,000 tonnes of flour.
The agency said last year Turkmenistan imported about 250,000 tonnes of wheat flour alone, mostly from the United States, Iran and Ukraine.
But potential imports this year may be threatened by a lack of hard-currency revenues since the country's natural gas industry, the major export earner, is in a state of chaos.

Turkmenistan is owed around $2 billion for previous gas exports. It halted deliveries to Western Europe this year as part of a troubled plan to set up a new distribution system, and already gas output has contracted by nearly half.

The State Statistics Committee said on Tuesday that due to the suspension of gas exports, Turkmenistan's trade surplus shrank in January-May to a mere $19 million from $374 million in the same period last year.
